sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Oversized Furniture and Home Decor

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (hybrid influenced by EU company law directives and international investment fund practice)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1996, as amended by 2004 protocol)
Luxembourg–France double tax treaty (1958, as amended)
Luxembourg–Germany double tax treaty (1959, as amended)
Luxembourg–China bilateral investment treaty (1998, in force)
OECD/G20 Inclusive Framework MLI agreement as applied to Luxembourg DTAs

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 creating the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as last amended by the Law of 25 July 2023; CSSF Regulation 12-02; Luxembourg Commercial Code (Articles 5 to 15 on partnerships); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS Law).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled copy of passport/identity document of each natural person UBO (25% or more) and each general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public / competent authority in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if origin is a Hague Convention state; otherwise Consular Legalization through the Luxembourg Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or recent register excerpt for any corporate general partner or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home jurisdiction company/commercial register (e.g., Companies House, Delaware Secretary of State, Trade and Companies Register)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, with French/German certified translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney authorizing the Luxembourg incorporation agent and local registered office provider to sign and file the SCSp deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent authority of the grantor(s)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, countersigned by Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential/business address for each UBO (utility bill, bank statement or official extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, bank or public administration in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not always apostilled; must be certified by the Luxembourg AML/CFT compliance officer

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Consent of the registered office provider in Luxembourg (acceptance of SCSp registered office address)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg corporate service provider or law firm
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized or signed original with specimen signature, no apostille required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit, CSSF sanctions and ministerial lists, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, EU restrictive measures, OFAC SDN list, and Interpol Red Notices for all UBOs, general partners and authorised signatories. The screening must be evidenced in the AML/KYC file under the Law of 12 November 2004 and kept for five years after the business relationship ends. A clear risk-based decision is required if any match or PEP status is identified, with enhanced due diligence where triggered.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) at rcs.lu / lbr.lu; electronic filing module 'eCompanies' used for name clearance and RCS registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be written in Latin characters; the official corporate name must contain the denomination 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp'. Names may be expressed in French, German or Luxembourgish; if the commercial name is in another language, a transliterated or translated form that is not misleading must be filed. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing RCS-registered entity or to an earlier reserved name; if it contains a personal or geographic element, it must not deceive the public.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant/dealing partner may submit an administrative appeal to the Registrar of the Luxembourg Business Registers within one month (30 days) from the rejection notice, citing Section 2 of the Law of 19 December 2002 and the RCS internal instructions. The appeal letter must include the exact proposed name, the SCSp registered office, the ISIC 4791 activity description, and reasons the name is distinctive and not contrary to public order. The registrar responds in writing within fifteen business days. If rejected again, an appeal may be brought before the Luxembourg administrative tribunal with the assistance of a Luxembourg-bar lawyer. A renewed name reservation application may be filed immediately after a formal withdrawal or court decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual registered office is accepted only if it consists of a physical Luxembourg street address of a law firm or licenced professional trust/corporate services provider, at which legal correspondence can be served and the statutory corporate documents are kept. For this online retail business (ISIC 4791 oversized furniture), a virtual office without inventory or employees will satisfy pre-incorporation registration formalities but will not automatically create Luxembourg tax substance; VAT and direct tax authorities will assess actual management and operational presence. If the entity uses only a mail-forwarding address, the tax authorities may challenge residency, and for VAT, a fixed establishment may not exist.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified as 10-15% annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Luxembourg RCS or by the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) if the registered office appears to be a mere letterbox or if VAT returns are inconsistent with reported turnover. The probability rises above 25% if the entity reports significant Luxembourg VAT credits or if the registered office provider is itself under supervision.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: LBR/RCS name reservation and initial clearance fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff published under the RCS Regulation; approximately EUR 25

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Electronic registration of the SCSp with RCS via eCompanies (déclaration de constitution)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory e-filing tariff (EUR 35-40; higher if paper filing)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the SCSp formation deed in the Luxembourg official gazette (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations - RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication fee set by the Ministry of Justice; approximate EUR 50

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RBE (UBO register) filing and validation fee for the SCSp beneficial owner statement
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: LBR regulated fee for RBE filing; approximate EUR 30

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial register extract / certificate of good standing for a corporate general partner (if not Luxembourg), notarized and apostilled
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Home jurisdiction company registry and competent notary/apostille authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Variable foreign registry tariff plus apostille fee; prevailing market benchmark USD 60-150

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille/consular legalization of UBO passport and address copies (four UBOs average)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs or Notary in the country of origin per UBO; Luxembourg consulate if legalization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular/apostille fee (approx. USD 50 per document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French/German translation of foreign commercial register excerpts and apostilled documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Scheduled translator tariff; approximate USD 150 per standard document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed drafting or power of attorney legalization for the SCSp formation (if private deed not used)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (total notarial fees including copy and registration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Grand-Ducal notarial fee regulation; approximate EUR 700-800 for non-real-estate partnership act

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg corporate lawyer AML/KYC client acceptance and UBO report preparation under Law of 12 November 2004
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard SCSp formation with AML clearance; EUR 1000-1600 fixed fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office support and statutory record-keeping for first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: EUR 60-100 per month depending on scope

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency for RCS/UBO rejection re-filing or extended custom's stamp duties
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Contingency based on statutory re-filing tariffs and administrative costs

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 1, 9, 10, 33-1 to 33-10 (société en commandite spéciale), together with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 September 2019 on the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de commerce et des sociétés, RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), 31/33 Boulevard Prince Henri, L-1724 Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership deed / charter of incorporation (acte de société) together with RCS form A (déclaration de renseignements), submitted electronically via the LBR RCSonline portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital applies to an SCSp. The partnership agreement freely determines the amount of capital or the contributions in cash or in kind; a limited partner may not make an industry (skills) contribution. No escrow account is required by Luxembourg law, but cash contributions must be actually paid into a bank account in the name of the SCSp, and a banker's certificate is customary evidence for the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD / MANAGING PARTNER RESOLUTION OF LU_SCSP

The sole general partner and manager of LU_SCSP, a Luxembourg société en commandite spéciale, acting under the amended Law of 10 August 1915, resolves: (1) The subscription of partnership interests set out in Annex A is accepted. (2) The registered office is adopted at [Registered Office Address], Luxembourg. (3) [Name] is appointed managing partner (gérant) with exclusive power to represent LU_SCSP. (4) [Name] is appointed AML/KYC officer. (5) The manager is authorised to file the deed with the RCS, open bank accounts, register for VAT and execute all regulatory filings. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search and Draft Name Protection
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – online register search at lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a free online search in the RCS to verify that the proposed name 'LU_SCSP' or the chosen trade name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name. Prepare a statement confirming availability and include the exact corporate form suffix 'société en commandite spéciale' or 'SCSp' in the draft deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused because it conflicts with a registered name, file a revised name request. Where a third party raises an opposition, apply to the tribunal d'arrondissement for a declaratory order of distinctiveness or correct the name and refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (if notarial deed chosen) or the partners by private deed with certified electronic signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SCSp partnership agreement in French, German or English, containing the corporate name, registered office in Luxembourg, corporate purpose (online retail of oversized furniture and home decor), duration, capital contributions, distribution waterfall, management and representation powers, general and limited partner rights, transfer restrictions and liquidation terms. Execute the deed with original wet-ink signatures before a Luxembourg notary or with compliant electronic signatures.
required_dossiers: Passports or national identity cards of all partners
Proof of residential address of all partners
Power of attorney if a representative signs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or adviser identifies material legal or KYC defects, amend the draft and re-execute. Any refusal based on incomplete partner due diligence may be cured by supplying updated identification and source-of-wealth evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution Verification and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg or EU/EEA credit institution; no government authority involved
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a bank account in the name of the SCSp and transfer the agreed cash contributions. Obtain a bank certificate or sworn statement confirming receipt of the subscribed capital and the beneficial owners. For in-kind contributions, obtain an independent valuation report and annex it to the partnership deed.
required_dossiers: Signed partnership agreement or final draft
Proof of funds and source of wealth
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank conducts enhanced due diligence and delays the account opening, provide additional documentation or approach another Luxembourg/EU bank. For in-kind contribution valuation queries, appoint a recognised Luxembourg auditor or certified expert to issue a revised report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration Filing and Corporate Birth
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS / Luxembourg Business Registers – RCSonline filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed partnership deed, RCS form A, registered office consent, manager appointment, bank capital certificate and partner identification documents to the LBR. Pay the state registration fee and obtain the RCS extract with the registration number. This registration provides third-party effectiveness for the SCSp.
required_dossiers: Registered office consent letter or lease agreement
Consent of managing partner to act as gérant
Bank capital certificate or in-kind valuation report
Copies of IDs of partners and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or correction request, respond within the prescribed 15-day deadline and submit amended documents. In case of formal refusal, appeal to the administrative tribunal of first instance within three months of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in RESA and UBO Register Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA) via LBR; LBR UBO register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure publication of the statutory extracts of the partnership agreement in the RESA. Then register the beneficial owners of the SCSp with the Luxembourg UBO register in accordance with the amended law of 13 January 2019. Keep the UBO data current and filed online.
required_dossiers: Copy of the partnership agreement or abstract
List of partners and ownership percentages
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication is refused, correct the abstract and resubmit. If the UBO filing is queried for incomplete data, file a rectification within 15 days; continued non-compliance may require an administrative notice to the public prosecutor.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Licensing, Tax Registration and Physical/Occupational Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Joint Social Security Centre (CCSS); Customs and Excise Administration; municipal fire commission; Inspectorate of Labour and Mines (ITM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File for a Luxembourg establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) if the SCSp operates an office, warehouse or delivery depot in Luxembourg. Register for VAT with the AEDT and obtain a valid VAT number. Register any employees with the CCSS and obtain an EORI number if the business imports goods. For physical premises, obtain a fire safety clearance from the municipal fire commission, a structural stability certificate for storage racking, and submit an occupational health and safety statement to the ITM. If the SCSp has no Luxembourg fixed establishment, document the exemption.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office and/or warehouse lease
Manager's identity document and clean criminal record
Business plan and commercial activity description
Structural load certificate for racking systems
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a permit is refused, provide supplementary technical documentation or amend the application. Administrative decisions may be appealed to the competent Minister within 15 days and thereafter to the administrative tribunal. For fire safety defects, request a reinspection by the municipal fire commission and remedy noted deficiencies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Direction générale des classes moyennes et de la consommation) and the competent municipal authority for possible establishment permits; no specific industrial licensing body applies to pure online retail under ISIC 4791.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable to pure online retail of oversized furniture; an autorisation d'établissement (business licence) may be required only if the SCSp operates a physical shop, warehouse or installation/service activity in Luxembourg.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from mandatory environmental impact assessment for e-commerce and furniture storage; the activity falls outside the EIA annexes if warehousing remains below applicable thresholds. If a large logistics facility is operated, a screening opinion from the Administration de l'environnement may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No sector-specific VOC, effluent or stack emissions limits apply to storage-only furniture e-commerce. General obligations under the amended Law of 9 June 2020 on waste management and municipal wastewater regulations must be observed; packaging waste must be managed in accordance with Luxembourg extended producer responsibility rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire safety commission is required for any premises accommodating employees or the public. A structural load certificate from a qualified engineer is required for high-rack furniture storage. The SCSp must submit an occupational health and safety declaration to the Inspectorate of Labour and Mines (ITM) and comply with workplace safety requirements under the Luxembourg Labour Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct income and corporate taxation; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT, registration duties and excise; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via lbr.lu for entity registration and issuance of the national identification matricule; primary e-filing portals: pfs.guichet.lu (direct tax), aedt.public.lu (VAT filings and guidance), and guichet.lu (central administrative procedures).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute the SCSp limited partnership agreement (contrat de société) between at least one general partner (commandité), who has unlimited joint liability, and at least one limited partner (commanditaire); no minimum capital is required and no notarial deed is mandatory unless the contribution comprises real estate. Step 2: File the incorporation record with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS) through lbr.lu so the partnership obtains the 13-digit national business matricule, which serves as the entity identification for corporate and tax registration. Step 3: Within one month of registration, file the beneficial ownership declaration in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE). Step 4: Apply for VAT registration with the AEDT using Form 1908 or via the LBR portal if annual taxable turnover exceeds EUR 35,000 (excluding VAT) or if voluntary OSS/IOSS registration is required; the AEDT issues the LU-prefixed VAT identification number. Step 5: Each foreign partner obtains a Luxembourg partner-specific matricule (natural person: numéro de dossier; legal person: matricule) only when the partner is resident in Luxembourg, has a Luxembourg permanent establishment, or is otherwise required to file a Luxembourg return; non-resident partners may otherwise rely on their home-jurisdiction TIN. Step 6: Confirm that the payment rails (Stripe and Affirm BNPL) are incorporated as SaaS counterparties of the SCSp and do not create a Luxembourg financial-sector licence or AML registration obligation for the furniture trade itself.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: The SCSp is a fiscal-transparency vehicle under Luxembourg law. It has no separate legal personality and is treated as a look-through entity for Luxembourg income tax purposes; the SCSp itself is not subject to corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC) or net wealth tax (IF). Each general and limited partner is taxed directly on its distributive share of net income: resident partners are fully taxed in Luxembourg; non-resident partners are taxed in Luxembourg only to the extent a Luxembourg permanent establishment or Luxembourg real estate is held, and no Luxembourg withholding tax applies on profit distributions by a transparent SCSp. For VAT purposes, however, the SCSp is an autonomous taxable person (assujetti) for supplies made in its own name and is therefore separately registered and files returns in its own VAT ID. Territorial scope: transparent allocation follows the partnership agreement and pushes income to the respective partners' jurisdictions; realisation income of a non-resident partner from disposing of SCSp interests is generally outside Luxembourg taxing power absent real property situated in Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Domestic law does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election; transparency of the SCSp is statutory and automatic under the Law of 23 July 2016 on commercial companies and the normal rules of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR). Available mechanisms: (a) an election under LIR Art. 175 allowing a partnership to opt for corporate (opaque) taxation, practically restricted to partnerships whose partners are all fully taxable Luxembourg corporate entities; (b) hybrid mismatch and ATAD rules (transposed by the Law of 21 December 2018) which require alignment where the SCSp is fiscally transparent in Luxembourg but opaque in a partner's home jurisdiction, together with a reporting obligation for qualifying hybrid mismatches and structured arrangements; (c) U.S. federal classification election under Treas. Reg. Section 301.7701-3 because the SCSp is not a per se corporation and may be classified by U.S. partners as a partnership or corporation; and (d) a Luxembourg VAT grouping election (assujetti unique) under Art. 62 of the VAT law enabling the SCSp and related enterprises to file as one VAT taxpayer.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée — TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover excluding VAT for the small-business exemption under Art. 57 of the Luxembourg VAT law; a SCSp whose turnover exceeds this threshold must mandatorily register for VAT. Non-resident suppliers without a Luxembourg establishment cannot invoke the small-business exemption. For intra-Community B2C distance sales of furniture to other EU Member States, an EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold (Art. 58(2) VAT law) applies: turnover below this amount is taxable in Luxembourg at 17%, while turnover above it must be declared through the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) portal in the Member State of the consumer. Imports of goods up to EUR 150 may be declared under the Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) scheme; import VAT on oversized goods entering through Luxembourg warehouses is due and may be deferred and deducted in the same return under Arts. 75 et seq. of the VAT law.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has not implemented real-time fiscal clearance, digitally stamped invoices, or continuous transaction controls comparable to Italy or Hungary. Electronic invoicing to central government buyers is mandatory via Peppol (EN 16931-compliant) under the B2G e-invoicing mandate; B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary, using Peppol, EDI or PDF, subject to authenticity and integrity requirements under Art. 81(3) of the VAT law. The EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) initiative, which will eventually mandate standardised B2B e-invoicing and digital VAT reporting, is being monitored but is not yet transposed in Luxembourg. VAT returns are filed electronically; OSS/IOSS schemes require periodic electronic declarations at the portal level.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of oversized furniture and home decor by the SCSp to non-EU destinations are eligible for the 0% export rate under Art. 53(I)(1) of the Luxembourg VAT law. Three cumulative conditions must be satisfied: (i) the goods are physically dispatched to a destination outside the EU; (ii) the goods leave the EU customs territory within 90 days of dispatch; and (iii) contemporaneous documentary proof of export is retained. Where the SCSp sells online to private consumers in the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Norway, the Gulf states, the United States or other third countries and ships from its Luxembourg warehouse, zero-rating is claimable. Ancillary services directly bundled into the supply and exported goods price, including freight, packing, handling and customs brokerage, also qualify for the 0% rate. Intra-EU B2B deliveries to registered dealers with confirmed VAT ID are zero-rated with EC Sales List filing; intra-EU B2C distance sales are taxed at destination via OSS. Domestic deliveries in Luxembourg remain standard-rated at 17%; a misfiled customer VAT ID or absence of transport evidence converts the supply into a taxable sale.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Export Single Administrative Document — EXS) with assigned Movement Reference Number (MRN) evidencing physical exit from the EU
Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB), or CMR consignment note demonstrating the transport route from the Luxembourg warehouse to the non-EU destination
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the oversize furniture items, quantities, values, and contractual place of delivery
Purchase and delivery records from the e-commerce platform confirming the customer as a non-EU consumer

Inward Remittance Certificate and bank settlement evidence (including Stripe or Affirm BNPL payout files) showing the sales proceeds credited to the SCSp's account, normally within 180 days of dispatch
Foreign customs import documentation or certificate of arrival from the destination country confirming physical receipt outside the EU
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT rigorously audits export zero-rating claims and documentation. If the export evidence is missing, inconsistent, or falsified, the VAT at 17% is retrospectively clawed back on the full supply value, together with statutory default interest and late-filing penalties; administrative penalties typically range from 10% to 50% of the VAT at risk depending on the degree of fault. Intentionally fraudulent zero-rating declarations constitute tax fraud under Art. 175 of the Luxembourg General Tax Act (Abgabenordnung) and potentially criminal fraud under the Luxembourg Criminal Code, carrying custodial sentences of up to five years and substantial criminal fines; the standard five-year limitation period for reassessment is extended to ten years in fraud cases. Although Luxembourg maintains no exchange-control statute mandating repatriation, the AEDT and AML compliance practice treat unremitted export proceeds beyond 180 days as an audit indicator warranting transfer-pricing and reality-of-sale review.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB) alongside the European Central Bank (ECB); the CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier) supervises credit institutions, payment institutions, and e-money institutions for AML/CFT and prudential conduct, while monetary and foreign-exchange policy competence rests with the Eurosystem for the euro area.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a fully liberal euro-area jurisdiction: current-account and capital-account convertibility are unrestricted under Articles 63-66 TFEU. There are no exchange controls, no prior authorisation for FX conversions, no restrictions on non-resident ownership of an SCSp, and no profit-remittance licensing requirements. EUR conversions for USD, GBP, and CNY are available at market rates through any CSSF-supervised bank. For a fiscally transparent SCSp, allocations of profit to non-resident partners do not normally attract Luxembourg withholding tax, and profit distributions may be settled freely via SEPA or SWIFT. The only administrative constraints are balance-of-payments statistical reporting to the BCL, AML/UBO filing obligations with the Luxembourg Business Registers, and substantiation of the tax-transparent character of the partnership before the receiving/scoring institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation of export receipts, no minimum retention period, and no mandatory conversion ratio into EUR. The SCSp may lawfully hold 100% of foreign-currency export proceeds in its Luxembourg accounts or in foreign-currency nostro balances for working capital and supplier settlement. However, all cross-border receipts must be correctly classified for BCL balance-of-payments statistics; the Luxembourg account-holding bank automatically reports customer transactions above materiality thresholds (commonly EUR 250,000 monthly cumulative), and the SCSp must provide trade-documentation support (invoices, transport evidence, customs declarations) to evidence that the flows relate to genuine retail-e-commerce trade in oversized furniture under ISIC 4791.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH for EEA-licensed and PSD2-passporting digital EMIs and payment institutions (for example Airwallex, Currenxie, Revolut Business, Wise Business, and MultiPass), which can open the SCSp account remotely and provide multi-currency IBANs, SWIFT/SEPA execution, and competitive EUR/USD/GBP/CNH conversion. These institutions are viable for the collection side of e-commerce treasury (Stripe settlements and BNPL disbursements) and for cross-border supplier payments. However, they are not credit institutions: they cannot issue documentary commercial letters of credit, provide committed working-capital or receivable-finance facilities, or deliver the same creditor protection and banking resolution stability as a Tier-1 Luxembourg bank. Non-EEA EMIs without an EU passport or without a Luxembourg branch cannot lawfully open accounts for the SCSp directly; their traffic must be intermediated by an EEA-licensed acquirer or partner bank. In all cases, the SCSp must satisfy the same RBE beneficial-ownership filing and source-of-funds evidencing obligations, and banks treating the SCSp as a non-financial partnership will apply individualised KYC rather than automated fintech onboarding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg AML/CFT law (Loi du 12 novembre 2004 modifiée) does not itself require an in-person meeting, and CSSF-accepted remote onboarding via video identification can satisfy Article 3 for most account structures. In practice, Tier-1 banks require for a contractually-structured SCSp without full legal personality: (i) positive identification of the general partner (gérant/associé commandité) and all authorised signatories; (ii) a recorded or high-grade video interview confirming the commercial rationale for a cross-border oversized-furniture e-commerce SCSp; and (iii) for non-EU beneficial owners, either a physical meeting at the bank's Luxembourg premises or notarised identification evidence with legalised/apostilled corporate documents. Remote-only onboarding is generally possible for EU/EEA residents using eIDAS-recognised electronic ID, but banks reserve discretion to require a first physical meeting where the SCSp has non-resident limited partners, zero paid-in capital, or opaque contractual profit-sharing clauses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp contractual structure lacking legal personality and potential concealment of underlying limited partners holding 25% or more of economic interest.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a structured UBO and corporate file: current extract from the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés); RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) confirmation; full partnership agreement (contrat de société) including all annexes identifying commanditaires; signed identity documents and passports of all UBOs; an ownership chart tracing each 25%-or-more economic interest to a natural person; Luxembourg tax-transparency opinion prepared by counsel; authenticated powers of attorney for the gérant; and a written source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declaration for each limited partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Zero or negligible paid-in capital and low substance profile flagged by transaction monitoring as a potential letterbox or conduit entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substance binder: signed commercial lease in Luxembourg; payroll or outsource contracts evidencing administrative staff; unique purchase and sales contracts for oversized furniture; logistics and warehousing agreements with freight forwarders; monthly board and gérant meeting minutes; the e-commerce platform's terms of service and merchant account evidence for Stripe and Affirm; forecasted cash-flow budget; and VAT (TVA) registration certificate demonstrating real registrable economic activity under ISIC 4791.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume fragmented B2C collections through Stripe payment facilitation and Affirm BNPL settlements creating uncertainty about the merchant of record and third-party settlement organisation (TPSO) exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full merchant agreements and settlement reports from Stripe and Affirm; merchant identification numbers and verified website/storefront printouts; PCI-DSS attestation from the payment stack; chargeback and refund policy documentation; a legal note proving that Affirm is the consumer lender and the SCSp is the merchant receiving net settlement; daily sales ledgers reconciling Stripe and Affirm deposits against the operational bank account; and a documented internal transaction-monitoring and AML/CFT procedure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large and periodic outbound supplier payments to Asian and emerging-market manufacturing jurisdictions (China, Vietnam, Turkey) using foreign-currency wiring and possible trade-based money-laundering red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction dossier per payment: commercial purchase contracts and proforma invoices; commercial invoices with item-level description of oversized furniture; packing lists; bills of lading, CMR waybills, or multimodal transport documents; customs declarations and customs-broker invoices; supplier KYC and sanctions-screening file; market-pricing benchmark against data sources for comparable furniture categories; LC drafts or SWIFT MT103 records; freight-forwarder contracts; and an internal reconciliation of inventory receipts versus invoice values.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partner ownership with US/UK payment rails and potential PEP, sanctions, or FATCA/CRS misreporting concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening output (EU, OFAC, UN) for all partners and beneficial owners; negative PEP declarations signed by natural persons; FATCA and CRS self-certification forms for each partner; tax residence certificates from each partner's jurisdiction; a copy of the RBE filing; articles showing the SCSp is not a US person and does not have US-source effectively-connected income; and an internal policy log demonstrating that no embargoed goods or sanctioned counterparties are involved in the furniture supply chain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For euro-area capital injections, route via SEPA Credit Transfer (TARGET2) to the SCSp's operative EUR IBAN; remittance information must state 'Capital contribution to [SCSp name] by [partner name] — [capital call reference]'. For non-EEA and USD/GBP/CNH injections, use SWIFT MT103/MT202 with a bank-recognised purpose code for equity capital contributions (for example ISO 20022 'EQUI' or the receiving bank's proprietary contribution code); field 70 must clearly read 'Equity contribution to Luxembourg SCSp — home furniture e-commerce'. The BCL balance-of-payments classification applied by the receiving bank will be direct-investment equity capital where the contributor holds 10% or more of partnership interests; portfolio-investment equity applies to smaller passive investors. The bank will require, before crediting the account, a current RCS extract, the partnership agreement, a capital-call resolution signed by the gérant, a source-of-funds declaration from the contributor, and full UBO/KYC files; transactions above EUR 250,000 in any calendar month are captured in the bank's automatic BCL external-statistics return, and, where requested, the SCSp must provide a breakdown by counterparty and country to support that return.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use the following clearing rails for trade settlements: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer for EU suppliers in EUR, referencing the VAT invoice and purchase-order number, with T+1 settlement via TARGET2; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for USD, GBP, CHF, and CNH commercial payments, cleared via the Luxembourg bank's correspondent network (Fedwire/CHIPS for USD, CIPS for CNY), with the purpose code reflecting goods trade and the underlying furniture purchase; (iii) irrevocable documentary Commercial Letters of Credit (at-sight or 30-120 days usance) issued by the BGL, Spuerkeess, or Société Générale under UCP 600 and ISBP 745 for large-value procurement from Asia, requiring commercial invoices, packing lists, transport documents (bills of lading, multimodal or CMR waybills), certificates of origin, and inspection certificates; and (iv) dedicated wallet-settlement rails for Stripe and Affirm: Stripe settles card/BNPL transaction batches in EUR to the SCSp's operating account via SEPA or SWIFT, while Affirm USA settlements may arrive via ACH to a US-dollar-denominated account or be converted to EUR under a standing FX order. Maintain separate treasury sub-ledgers for supplier trade payments, platform settlement charges, and BNPL receivable advances to preserve audit integrity and support the BCL statistical reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CNH, EUR/CHF) matched to underlying receivable and payable maturities
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for onshore CNY and other restricted or illiquid currencies required for Chinese and Vietnamese supplier procurement
FX swaps (swap de devises) for intra-month liquidity alignment between USD/GBP settlement receipts from Stripe and Affirm and EUR operating expenditures
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) linked to committed working-capital or trade-finance facilities where the SCSp borrows in foreign currency
Long-only FX options and zero-cost collar structures permitted when there is a demonstrable underlying commercial exposure in the oversized-furniture e-commerce trade cycle

All hedging transactions must be executed with a CSSF-licensed credit institution or investment firm under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement, must respect EMIR mandatory clearing and risk-mitigation thresholds, and must be separately recorded for BCL balance-of-payments and CRS/FATCA transparency purposes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of RCS registration data (Confirmation annuelle au RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following the anniversary date of the RCS registration; the exact date is generated by the LBR online portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late confirmation triggers a formal reminder and an administrative fine of up to EUR 5,000. Continued non-confirmation for more than 12 months may lead to an administrative strike-off procedure initiated by the Public Prosecutor's Office.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposit with the RCSL (required only if the SCSp exceeds the statutory audit threshold)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the close of the financial year (e.g., by 31 July for a 31 December year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file within the statutory period exposes the general partner to criminal penalties and administrative fines of up to EUR 10,000; persistent default may also trigger deregistration from the RCSL and loss of good-standing certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership record update with the RBE (upon any change; no recurring annual filing unless information changes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of any change in beneficial ownership; annual review should be aligned with the RCS annual confirmation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate or late UBO declarations subject the general partner and manager to criminal fines ranging from EUR 250 to EUR 1,250 per confirmed violation, and may additionally impair the entity's RCS standing and administrative good-standing profile.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The SCSp is required to appoint a Luxembourg statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) if, for two consecutive financial years, it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds: balance-sheet total of EUR 4.4 million, net turnover of EUR 8.8 million, and average workforce of 50 employees. A separate audit may also be mandated under the AIFM/UCITS framework when the SCSp is used as a regulated investment fund vehicle.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial register and accounting (as amended, including the Law of 23 July 2016); IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted for voluntary use and generally required for consolidated or regulated fund structures.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The RBE does not impose a standalone annual UBO filing absent a change of beneficial ownership. However, the general partner must maintain a complete register of partners at the registered office, verify its accuracy at least once per year, align it with the RCS annual confirmation date, and file any change of beneficial ownership with the RBE within one month.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General Partner Management Decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 - USD 2,500 per year for a licensed registered office and corporate agent in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,500 - USD 18,000 for a clean small-to-middle-market SCSp audit under Luxembourg GAAP

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% maximum aggregate Luxembourg CIT rate for resident corporate partners (Luxembourg City, 2024), composed of 17% corporate income tax plus 7% solidarity surcharge plus municipal business tax (approx. 6.75% Luxembourg City). The SCSp itself is fiscally transparent and is not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax at entity level.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is pass-through eligible: 0% CIT at entity level. Corporate partners may benefit from the Luxembourg participation exemption (100% exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains derived from a 10% or greater qualifying holding), the IP box regime (80% exemption of qualifying IP income), and investment tax credits. No statutory tax holidays apply to online retail; the effective rate for a qualifying corporate partner can be reduced to 0% for exempt participation income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 270 / 470 suite (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, l'impôt commercial communal et l'impôt sur la fortune) filed electronically via the Administration des contributions directes (ACD) through eTax / MyGuichet.lu.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; quarterly advance payments of corporate income tax and municipal business tax are generally due in March, June, September, and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Default deadline is within six months after the end of the financial year (e.g., 30 June for a taxpayer with a 31 December year-end). Electronic filing through the ACD portal automatically extends the deadline to 31 December of the following calendar year. Extensions may be requested but are not automatic.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the SCSp, registered number with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), registered office address, e-mail, and contact details of the authorised representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Luxembourg registered address as filed with the RCS. If the SCSp has no Luxembourg office, attach a statement identifying the legal representative in Luxembourg and the address for service of tax documents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 by Legal Form and Tax Status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate the legal form as Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) and mark the tax classification as fiscally transparent. If the SCSp has made an election to be treated as taxable for Luxembourg corporate income tax purposes, state the election and attach the relevant approval.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must not be reported as taxable shareholders in the SCSp return. The return should state that the entity is transparent and that each partner will be taxed on its allocable share according to the partnership agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the financial year, accounting reference period, and confirmation that annual accounts have been filed with the RCS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide a full accounting period reconciliation. Non-resident partners with taxable Luxembourg permanent establishments must ensure that the allocated profit is consistent with the Luxembourg branch accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 by Turnover and Commercial Revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from the online retail of oversized furniture and home decor, including delivery charges, assembly services, insurance, and any ancillary e-commerce services, computed in EUR.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All Luxembourg-sourced e-commerce revenue must be reported. For non-resident partners without a Luxembourg permanent establishment, the revenue is disclosed only for transparency and income allocation purposes; it is not automatically taxable in Luxembourg, but the LTA will scrutinise the allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 by Related Party Transactions and TP Annex
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List all transactions with related enterprises: purchases from group suppliers, sales to group warehouses, logistics fees, commission payments, intercompany loans, and management charges. Attach the Luxembourg transfer pricing annex and provide the master file/local file when the applicable threshold is triggered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners that are part of a multinational group must ensure the Luxembourg SCSp retains a full transfer pricing documentation file, including contemporaneous comparables, even if the partner itself is outside Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 by Taxable Result and Partner Allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of commercial net profit to taxable result, allocation of the taxable result among general and limited partners in accordance with the contribution schedule, and statement of any loss carry-forward claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the partnership profit allocation schedule. For non-resident corporate partners, clearly identify the share of profit attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment. If the partner claims relief under a double tax treaty, the form should identify the applicable DTA and confirm that no Luxembourg PE exists.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an administrative fine of up to EUR 25,000, a late-filing surcharge of 10% of the tax due (increased to 20% if the return is not remedied within 30 days after formal notice), and late-payment interest of 0.6% per month (7.2% per annum). Deliberately false declarations may additionally trigger criminal prosecution under Articles 396 et seq. LIR with fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment from one to five years.
